messages:
jamie: FYI we saw a cross-region spike in mTLS failures after the RBAC cleanup this morning. proxies in eu-west and ap-southeast logged session ticket unwrap denies and some client cert validation failures. sample: 

2026-03-25T04:07:03Z proxy-eu-04 cert_lookup: found wrapped_ticket s3://session-keys/eu/wrapped-abc
2026-03-25T04:07:03Z proxy-eu-04 kms_unwrap: DecryptDenied principal=arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/key-handler key=alias/sessions-eu
2026-03-25T04:07:03Z proxy-eu-04 tls_resume_fail: ERR_SSL_SESSION_TICKET_INVALID

olga: which PR changed the KMS scoping? I saw housecleaning PR #5102 that removed old key permissions.

deploy-bot: Audit: CloudTrail shows 157 KMS:DecryptDenied events for principals matching role:key-* between 04:05:00 and 04:08:30 in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Related PR: #5102 (rbac/kms-cleanup).

reza: looks like the PR scoped alias names to alias/sessions (no region suffix) but runtime expects region-specific aliases (alias/sessions-eu, alias/sessions-apac). alias naming drift meant runtime consumers lost access.

ops-oncall: immediate mitigation: attach temporary allow for alias/sessions-eu and alias/sessions-apac to the key-handler and cert-fetcher roles (30m), pause live key rotations, and roll proxies (canary then full) to clear cached bad certs. applied temp allow at 04:12.

deploy-bot: Verification: KMS:Decrypt success observed for role:key-handler at 04:12:41. resume rate on canary improved from 58% -> 96%.

jamie: root cause: RBAC scoping change + alias naming mismatch -> wrapped key unwrap fails -> TLS resume/client cert validate errors -> increased full handshakes and latency.

olga: short-term follow-ups: 1) revert or fix alias scoping in PR #5102 and add region aliases back, 2) add infra test that simulates KMS Deny for each key consumer before merging alias-scoping changes, 3) add alert: KMS:DecryptDenied > 0 for any role tagged cert-consumer in 5m -> page eng-security + oncall.

reza: longer-term: make unwrap path resilient: on KMS Deny fall back to completing a fresh TLS handshake rather than dropping connection; consider a conservative in-memory cache of recently unwrapped session keys (TTL 30s) to survive transient KMS flaps (security review required). also produce a canonical mapping of KMS aliases -> consumers and enforce CI validation that RBAC PRs cannot remove access for listed consumers without explicit ack.

ops-oncall: compliance request: record PR approval chain and attach test evidence. I'll update secure-deploy checklist to require a key-consumer inventory stamp and add CT query snippets to the incident ticket.

olga: CloudTrail query I used: 
EventName = "Decrypt" OR EventName = "Decrypt*" | where eventSource == "kms.amazonaws.com" and recipientAccountId == "111222333444" | where eventTime between ("2026-03-25T04:00:00Z","2026-03-25T04:20:00Z")

jamie: assigning owners: @reza fix alias mapping + PR; @olga draft postmortem & include CT snippets; @ops-oncall add alert + dashboard (session_resume_rate by region). closing thread once postmortem is filed. :thumbsup:
